title: Europe’s summer holidays are over
gist: The 2026 European wildfire season forced more than 370,000 evacuations and burned over 254,000 hectares, with France staging one of its largest peacetime civilian evacuations and Gironde's prefect telling tourists not to come. Sema Karaman argues state tourism agencies are spending hundreds of millions of euros manufacturing peak-summer demand in exactly the regions the European Environment Agency flags as most exposed to heat, fire and water scarcity, and that the model must shift toward shoulder seasons — or to lower absolute volumes.

insights.claim: More than 370,000 residents and holidaymakers have been evacuated across southern and western Europe since the start of summer 2026, with dozens of simultaneous fires burning over 254,000 hectares.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: Baseline magnitude for pricing recurring European summer disruption risk in travel, insurance and regional infrastructure.
insights.quote: More than 370,000 residents and holidaymakers have been forced to evacuate across southern and western Europe since summer began.
insights.locator: Extreme temperatures have scorched the continent

insights.claim: France's July 2026 wildfires in Gironde and Landes triggered one of the largest peacetime civilian evacuation operations in the country's history, removing nearly 250,000 people from homes and holiday accommodation.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: Evacuation at this scale is a state-capacity event, not just a tourism inconvenience — implies rising French public spending on emergency response.
insights.quote: nearly 250,000 people removed from their homes and holiday accommodation in the southwestern departments of Gironde and Landes
insights.locator: The reality, as of last week, is rather different

insights.claim: A regional French official has actively told tourists not to travel to her department, an unprecedented inversion of the state's normal promotional posture.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: When a destination's own government issues stay-away messaging, forward bookings and regional hospitality revenue take a direct hit.
insights.quote: Sophie Brocas, prefect of Gironde, has urged tourists “not to come”.
insights.locator: The reality, as of last week, is rather different

insights.claim: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez attributed the 2026 wildfire outbreak directly to the increasingly extreme impacts of climate change, while President Macron called the fires completely unprecedented.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: Head-of-government attribution to climate change raises the odds of EU-level adaptation funding and fire-prevention mandates.
insights.quote: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez attributing the outbreak to the “increasingly extreme impacts of climate change”

themes.theme: Tourism demand is publicly manufactured, not natural

insights.claim: European tourism demand is not simply the passive consequence of beautiful coastlines but is actively manufactured by state agencies spending millions on advertising, influencer partnerships and international campaigns.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: Reframes tourist volumes as a policy lever governments can dial down — meaning southern European visitor numbers are politically, not just climatically, determined.
insights.quote: Yet publicly funded tourism agencies spend millions on advertising, influencer partnerships and international campaigns to attract travellers.
insights.locator: Europe’s tourism economy is often presented

insights.claim: State tourism promotion budgets are substantial: Turespaña's 2024 budget exceeded €103m with over a third for promotion, Atout France received a €24.66m public-service subsidy in 2025, and Italy's ENIT allocated €19.37m to promotion plus €10m to marketing in its 2026 budget.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: Quantifies the fiscal subsidy underpinning peak-season tourism flows — a budget line vulnerable to redirection if climate politics shift.
insights.quote: the 2024 budget of Turespaña, the public body responsible for managing Spain’s tourism brand, exceeded €103m, with slightly more than one-third devoted to promotion
insights.locator: Atout France is a public-private body

insights.claim: The Greek National Tourism Organisation invested a reported €34m across seven advertising campaigns in 35 international markets between 2021 and 2023 plus €30m in co-advertising, and in April 2026 launched a three-month TikTok and YouTube campaign across five European markets reaching an estimated 19m users.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: Greece is the clearest case of taxpayer-funded demand generation flowing into social platforms — a state ad spend stream for TikTok and YouTube.
insights.quote: Between 2021 and 2023, the Greek National Tourism Organisation reportedly invested €34m in seven advertising campaigns across 35 international markets, alongside €30m in co-advertising with international partners.
insights.locator: Greece is perhaps the clearest example

insights.claim: In 2025 France welcomed a record 102m international tourists generating €77.5bn in receipts while Spain received 96.8m tourists who spent €134.7bn, with Italy at €56.7bn of foreign spending and Greece at 43.3m arrivals and €23.6bn in travel receipts.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: Sizes the revenue at risk from a climate-driven collapse in peak-summer Mediterranean travel — Spain's €134.7bn is the largest single exposure.
insights.quote: Spain received 96.8m international tourists, who spent €134.7bn.

insights.claim: Greece is structurally the most exposed European tourism economy because non-residents accounted for 83.8 per cent of all nights spent in registered tourist accommodation, leaving no domestic buffer if foreign demand falls.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: Greek hospitality and related sovereign revenue have the thinnest cushion against a climate-driven demand shock — highest beta to the theme.
insights.quote: non-residents accounted for 83.8 per cent of all nights spent in registered tourist accommodation
insights.locator: Greece is especially dependent on international demand

insights.claim: UK residents made 94.6m visits abroad in 2024 with Spain the top destination at 17.8m visits, ahead of France at 9.3m and Italy at 4.8m, making British outbound travel a major transmission channel for Mediterranean climate disruption.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: UK travel operators and airlines with Spain-heavy route maps carry concentrated exposure to Mediterranean heat events.
insights.quote: UK residents made 94.6m visits abroad in 2024, with Spain the most visited country with 17.8m visits, followed by France with 9.3m and Italy with 4.8m
insights.locator: And the UK, of course, provides a great number

themes.theme: Redistribution, not reduction: the shoulder-season trap

insights.claim: Shifting travel to spring and autumn may reduce heat exposure but risks simply extending the peak season, so climate change is likely to redistribute European tourism geographically and seasonally rather than reduce it.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: Expect longer Mediterranean seasons and new northern hotspots rather than falling total volumes — a duration trade, not a demand-destruction trade.
insights.quote: Climate change may therefore redistribute European tourism rather than reduce it.
insights.locator: If tourist numbers are not carefully managed

insights.claim: In the most saturated and climate-exposed destinations, absolute reduction in tourism volumes may be unavoidable, requiring a managed transition away from a model built on ever-rising visitor numbers.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: A policy-driven cap on volumes in flagship destinations would hit short-term rental platforms, cruise operators and hotel capacity plans.
insights.quote: In the most saturated and climate-exposed destinations, less tourism overall may have to be part of the answer.
insights.locator: In the most saturated and climate-exposed destinations

insights.claim: Tourism policy should be judged not by visitor numbers or revenue but by resident welfare, year-round employment security and environmental limits, including the relative cost of drought and wildfire management.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: A metric change of this kind precedes regulation — watch for short-term rental restrictions and tourist levies replacing growth targets.
insights.quote: The measure of success should be resident welfare, secure year-round employment and respect for environmental limits.
insights.locator: Tourism policy can no longer be judged

insights.claim: The European Commission's Transition Pathway for Tourism and national strategies already commit to less seasonal dependence, but in practice these commitments have not progressed beyond words on paper.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: Stated EU tourism-transition policy is not yet an investable signal; the implementation gap means status quo persists until a forcing event.
insights.quote: Yet in practice, all too often these commitments have not progressed beyond words on paper.
insights.locator: The European Commission’s Transition Pathway for Tourism

insights.claim: Southern Europe's tourism is heavily concentrated in July and August in exactly the region the European Environment Agency identifies as most exposed to extreme heat, wildfire and water scarcity.
insights.speaker: Sema Karaman
insights.so_what: The seasonal and geographic overlap of peak demand with peak physical risk is the structural flaw in the European tourism model.
insights.quote: tourism remains heavily concentrated in the summer, with July and August the peak months
